message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have $536 and a pink monopoly with four houses on each property. I am currently on the mortgaged Illinois Avenue owned by p1. p1 has a dangerous dark blue monopoly with Park Place at three houses and Boardwalk at four houses. p3 is bankrupt.

p4 has $1392 and a light blue monopoly with four houses each, plus railroads. The bank holds only one house and twelve hotels. I must avoid selling or building on my pink properties, since that would free houses for p1 to use on Park Place. Park Place needs one more house to reach four, while Boardwalk at four houses is too dangerous.

Building a hotel on one pink property would return four houses to the bank. That would free houses for p1 to use on Park Place and the yellows. I must avoid building hotels.

Hotel upgrades on the pink properties would raise rent by only $200 each. The four houses returned to the bank would let p1 build a fourth house on Park Place, raising its rent from $1100 to $1300. Brown monopolies are mortgaged and cannot be upgraded.

Red, yellow, and green monopolies are incomplete or mortgaged, so p1 cannot build on them. Only the dark blue set is fully available for upgrading.

I can barely afford the $1100 rent on Park Place. Selling all twelve houses from my pink properties would yield $600, combined with my $536 cash, giving me about $1136 total. If p1 builds a fourth house and raises rent to $1300, I would need to mortgage my pink properties for roughly $440, but I must sell all houses first before mortgaging.

Boardwalk at four houses costs $1700. Even liquidating everything would only yield about $1576, so that is impossible to survive. I will not unmortgage any properties either, since partial monopolies offer no benefit. I can trade with p1 and p4.

I am weighing whether to propose a trade. p4's light blue properties are not a major threat, since my cash can cover their rent. The real danger is p1, who has only $58 and is on New York Avenue. I must choose an action for this turn.

I have not rolled the dice yet. This is the optional post-turn phase, so I will end my turn without building, selling, or unmortgaging. I briefly considered trading with p4 to hurt p1 or buying Park Place from p1, but those ideas are unworkable.

I considered trading Tennessee to p4 to complete their orange monopoly, but that would give them a second strong set. I also thought about giving p4 my Pennsylvania Railroad, which would raise their railroad rent from $50 to $100 and bring in cash.

I rejected trading my Pennsylvania Railroad to p4. A three-railroad set is not enough to beat the dark blues, and that trade would only help p4 more.

I also considered trading with p1 to break their dark blue monopoly. I could offer cash or my pink properties, but Boardwalk at four houses is too valuable to give up, and my pink monopoly is worth more to me than breaking p1's set. Tennessee and the PRR are too weak to offer in exchange.

I considered offering cash plus another property to buy one dark blue from p1 and break their monopoly. I am unsure if the game allows trading properties that have houses on them, since the trade schema only lists cash, properties, and get-out-of-jail cards.

I now suspect the engine would reject trades involving improved properties. I also realized that even if p1 could be convinced to trade away a dark blue, they would never accept a deal that breaks their only winning monopoly. I briefly considered trying to acquire Kentucky or Atlantic and Ventnor from p1 to block them from building monopolies, but they only have $58 and cannot easily unmortgage those properties anyway.

I will keep my Get Out of Jail card to remain in jail and avoid the dark blue monopolies. I must not give p1 cash, since that would let them unmortgage Marvin and build yellows. The only viable action is to end my turn.

Hoteling is strictly harmful. It costs $100 and only adds $200 rent on one property, while freeing houses for p1 to upgrade Park Place. Selling houses would reduce my own rent, making it harder for me to bankrupt p1. Unmortgaging the PRR or Tennessee is also unprofitable, since neither would complete a monopoly and the rent would be too low.
